name: Retail Banking
era: Modern form since ~17th c. goldsmith-bankers; deposit banking much older

chain.relation_note: First entry in the Atlas. The chain grows from here.

suggested_next.why: The software rails every bank runs on — who sells the picks and shovels?
Visa/Mastercard sit on the same money flow and run a pure toll-booth.
Same 'float' mechanic as deposits, different wrapper — the first cross-link.

one_line: Buy money cheap from depositors, sell it dear to borrowers, and live on the gap.

engine.inputs: Deposits — other people's money, entrusted cheaply
engine.transformation: Pools deposits, holds a fraction as capital, lends the rest out many times over
engine.outputs: Loans — the same money, sold as credit at a higher rate
engine.money_in: Interest and fees from borrowers; card, account and overdraft fees
engine.money_out: Interest paid to depositors; operating cost; loan losses
engine.the_spread: loan rate − deposit rate  (the Net Interest Margin)
engine.leverage_point: Hold ~10% as capital, lend the rest — roughly 10× the capital base

unit.unit_economics: A dollar deposited at ~0.5% funds a loan at ~7%; the ~6.5pt gross spread, minus losses and cost, is the margin. Figures illustrative.
unit.what_one_unit_produces: Not just interest — a customer relationship that can be cross-sold cards, mortgages, and advice at higher margin.

plays.tagline: Raise loan rates fast. Raise deposit rates slow.

flow.step_desc: Loan rates jump the same day; deposit rates crawl up over months.
The bank keeps the widening gap before it has to pass raises on.

plays.the_move: Loans reprice at a sprint; deposits reprice at a walk. The delay itself is the money.
plays.in_the_wild: In the 2022–23 hiking cycle, US loan yields rose faster than deposit costs — 'loan betas beat deposit betas' — fattening margins until deposit costs caught up.
plays.watch_out: Eventually depositors demand their raise. Margins peak, then compress.

plays.tagline: Boring rates. The real money leaks in from the sides.

flow.step_desc: Headline rates are unremarkable — nothing to see.
Overdraft, account, ATM, card and wire fees pour in from every side.
Non-interest income becomes the profit engine, not the spread.

plays.the_move: Don't win on the spread — win on the fine print. Dozens of small fees fill the moat.
plays.in_the_wild: US retail banking has historically drawn a large share of revenue from non-interest income — fees small and frequent enough that customers barely notice them adding up.
plays.watch_out: Fee income is politically fragile — regulators love to cap overdraft and 'junk' fees.

plays.tagline: Own one narrow lane. Charge a premium for the expertise.

flow.step_desc: Auto loans, small-business, equipment leasing — one segment, deeply known.
Underwrite risk competitors can't read; lend where they won't.
Charge more because you understand the borrower better than anyone.

plays.the_move: Skip the scale war. Go an inch wide and a mile deep, and price the expertise.
plays.in_the_wild: Community banks lean on this — accepting higher risk on borrowers they personally know in exchange for higher yield.
plays.watch_out: Concentration. If your one lane hits a pothole, the whole book feels it.

plays.tagline: Outbid everyone on savings. Pull cash in fast, then deploy.

flow.step_desc: Post a top-of-market savings or CD rate.
Cash arrives faster than organic growth ever could.
Turn funding into higher-yielding loans and earn the spread.

plays.the_move: Buy funding aggressively when you need liquidity now — speed over cost.
plays.in_the_wild: Post-pandemic, national high-yield platforms let banks vacuum up deposits with a rate — but that funding is 'hot': it chases the next best rate and leaves as fast.
plays.watch_out: Rate-shoppers aren't loyal. Elevated deposit costs squeeze the very margin you chased.

plays.tagline: One shiny product to get you in. Then bundle you in for life.

flow.step_desc: A standout product — a high-yield savings account — gets you through the door.
Checking, card, mortgage, investments — bundled with relationship pricing.
Each added product makes leaving costlier; you stop shopping around.

plays.the_move: The rate is bait. The profit is everything they sell you afterward.
plays.in_the_wild: A standard tactic: tie every new loan to a household checking account — integrated bundles cut churn and lock in the relationship.
plays.watch_out: For the customer: convenience quietly costs the best rate on each individual product. For the bank: aggressive cross-sell can tip into scandal (see Wells Fargo).

mechanics_summary.note: Profit is the gap between a cheap input price and a dear output price.
Hold other people's money in the gap between receiving and paying it out.
Leverage a thin capital base into a large asset book; regulated by ratio.
Lose on the lure to win on everything sold after it.
Sit on a flow and charge a small fee each time value passes.

origin.what_problem_forced_it: Merchants needed somewhere safe to store gold. Goldsmiths issued paper receipts for deposits; when they noticed not everyone withdrew at once, they began lending out receipts against gold they held — inventing fractional-reserve lending and, with it, the spread.

operator.name: A. P. Giannini, Bank of Italy / Bank of America
operator.what_they_did: Opened banking to working-class immigrants ignored by elite banks in early-1900s San Francisco; lent on character and small deposits, and famously lent to rebuild after the 1906 earthquake. Turned the 'underserved, not unworthy' niche into the largest bank in the country.
operator.outcome: Bank of America became, for a time, the world's largest commercial bank.

counterexample.name: Wells Fargo cross-sell scandal (2016)
counterexample.what_they_did: Pushed the Cross-Sell Trap past the line — employees under quota pressure opened millions of accounts customers never authorized.
counterexample.why_it_broke: The play depends on customer trust; manufacturing fake demand destroyed it, drew billions in fines, and capped the bank's growth by regulators for years.

unknowns: Exact current NIM varies widely by bank, year, and rate environment — not pinned here.
Non-interest income share differs by institution; stated only as 'a large share'.
Deposit/loan beta figures for 2022–23 are directional, not sourced to a specific filing in this entry.

recall.glyph_prompt: Picture two arrows off the same starting line: the loan arrow shoots up fast, the deposit arrow crawls. The widening wedge between them is the profit.
three_questions: Where does a bank's money come in, and where does it go out?
What single equation is the whole business? (loan rate − deposit rate)
Name two ways a bank widens or defends that spread.

scale.metric: net operating revenue of all FDIC-insured US banks
scale.basis: industry (all US insured banks, not retail-only)
scale.note: Net interest income $738.3B + noninterest income $337.8B. Covers all insured banks, so it overstates retail banking alone.
